title: When a Group Learns to Disagree
title_ja: 意見の違いを学ぶグループ
fact_notes: 人物・制度・具体的な出来事は架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査・統計・実証結果を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional school committee was asked to decide whether a spare classroom should be converted into a quiet study space or a room for collaborative projects.
sentences.ja: 架空の学校委員会は空き教室を静かな学習室にするか共同活動室にするか決めるよう求められた。

sentences.en: At the first meeting, several students spoke strongly in favor of the option they preferred, while others remained silent throughout the discussion.
sentences.ja: 最初の会議で自分の希望案を強く支持する生徒もいれば議論中ずっと沈黙する生徒もいた。

sentences.en: The chairperson interpreted the absence of objections as evidence that most members agreed with the proposal currently receiving the greatest attention.
sentences.ja: 議長は反対がないことを最も注目された案への多数の賛同の証拠と解釈した。

sentences.en: However, a member later explained that she had not felt comfortable interrupting the speakers to express a concern.
sentences.ja: しかし後に一人が懸念を述べるため発言者を遮ることに抵抗があったと説明した。

sentences.en: Before the second meeting, the committee collected anonymous written suggestions from its members about the two possible uses of the classroom.
sentences.ja: 第二回会議の前に二つの教室用途について匿名の意見を委員から集めた。

sentences.en: Several responses emphasized needs that had received little attention, including difficulties finding a quiet place after school and problems arranging group meetings.
sentences.ja: 放課後に静かな場所を見つけにくいことやグループ会議の調整など、注目されていなかった必要を数件が強調した。

sentences.en: The committee discovered that the disagreement involved different experiences rather than merely a contest between two strongly expressed opinions.
sentences.ja: 意見の違いは強く述べられた二意見の競争だけでなく異なる経験に関係すると分かった。

sentences.en: It therefore asked each member to explain the circumstances that made a particular option valuable before discussing which plan should be adopted.
sentences.ja: そこで採用案を議論する前に各案を価値あるものにする状況を説明するよう求めた。

sentences.en: Several students suggested dividing the day into scheduled periods of quiet study and collaborative work, although this arrangement would require clear rules about transitions.
sentences.ja: 静かな自習と共同作業の時間帯を設ける案が出たが、切り替えに明確なルールが必要だった。

sentences.en: Others pointed out that the room might not be suitable for every kind of project and that a schedule would need to reflect practical limitations.
sentences.ja: 全種類の活動に適するとは限らず、日程には実用的制約を反映する必要があるという指摘も出た。

sentences.en: Rather than claiming that the combined proposal satisfied everyone, the members described remaining disadvantages and suggested a temporary trial.
sentences.ja: 統合案が全員を満足させると主張せず、残る欠点を説明し試行を提案した。

sentences.en: They agreed to collect further feedback before recommending a permanent arrangement.
sentences.ja: 恒久的な仕組みを提案する前に追加の意見を集めることにした。

sentences.en: The chairperson began to recognize that a meeting could appear harmonious without providing its participants with equal opportunities to influence the outcome.
sentences.ja: 会議は調和しているように見えても参加者に結果への平等な影響機会を与えるとは限らないと議長は認識し始めた。

sentences.en: Asking people to explain their experiences made the sources of disagreement clearer, even when their preferred solutions remained different.
sentences.ja: 希望する解決策が異なるときも経験を説明することで対立の原因がより明確になった。

sentences.en: The committee did not assume that every disagreement would eventually disappear through discussion.
sentences.ja: 議論ですべての対立が消えるとは考えなかった。

sentences.en: Instead, it developed a procedure for deciding how to proceed while acknowledging concerns that could not be fully resolved.
sentences.ja: 完全に解決できない懸念を認めながら進め方を決める手順を作った。

sentences.en: The example illustrates why respectful collaboration should not be evaluated solely by the absence of visible conflict.
sentences.ja: この例は尊重ある協力を目に見える対立がないことだけで評価すべきでない理由を示す。

sentences.en: A discussion may be more productive when participants are able to express a relevant disagreement without fear of interrupting an apparently successful meeting.
sentences.ja: 成功しているように見える会議を遮ることを恐れず関連する反対意見を表せると議論はより有益になり得る。

sentences.en: The purpose of listening is not always to arrive at identical preferences, but to understand the needs that a decision must take into account.
sentences.ja: 傾聴の目的は常に同一の好みに到達することでなく、決定が考慮すべき必要を理解することである。

sentences.en: For the committee, learning to cooperate included learning to disagree openly and constructively.
sentences.ja: 委員会にとって協力を学ぶことは率直かつ建設的に意見を異にすることを含んだ。

options: How to use a spare classroom.
How to repair the library roof.
Some concerns were not expressed aloud.
questions.explanation_ja: 懸念が発言されなかった。

options: Only one student had used the room.
Different practical needs behind the preferences.
Using the room exclusively for meetings.
Scheduling different activities at different times.
questions.explanation_ja: 時間帯で用途を分ける。

options: The compromise still had disadvantages to examine.
The name of the next chairperson.

questions.prompt: What did the committee avoid assuming?
questions.explanation_ja: 対立がすべてなくなるとは考えない。

options: Open disagreement can strengthen respectful cooperation.
Conflict should be hidden from decision makers.
questions.explanation_ja: 意見の違いを率直に扱う。

paraphrases.source: At the first meeting, several students spoke strongly in favor of the option they preferred, while others remained silent throughout the discussion.
paraphrases.rewrite: Some members argued strongly for their choice, whereas others said nothing.

paraphrases.source: It therefore asked each member to explain the circumstances that made a particular option valuable before discussing which plan should be adopted.
paraphrases.rewrite: They asked members to describe why an option mattered before choosing a plan.

paraphrases.source: Several students suggested dividing the day into scheduled periods of quiet study and collaborative work, although this arrangement would require clear rules about transitions.
paraphrases.rewrite: They suggested separate time periods, even though transitions would require rules.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 時間分けにはルールが必要。

paraphrases.source: The purpose of listening is not always to arrive at identical preferences, but to understand the needs that a decision must take into account.
paraphrases.rewrite: Listening aims to understand decision-relevant needs rather than necessarily make everyone prefer the same thing.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 同一の好みではなく必要を理解。

discourse.role_ja: 対立を認めた決定手順。
